name: Penang Bridge International Marathon
short_description: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is a full marathon, half marathon and 10 km race on Sunday 13 December 2026, starting at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan, Penang, and run over the Penang Second Bridge.
ai_summary: The Penang Bridge International Marathon is a road race scheduled for Sunday 13 December 2026. Since 2024 it has started and finished at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan, on the Penang mainland, with the course run out and back over the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah Bridge (the Penang Second Bridge). It offers three distances: a full marathon (42.195 km), a half marathon (21.1 km) and a 10 km run. The event is organised by the Penang State Tourism Development office with support from PETACE.

core_facts.organizer: Penang State Tourism Development office (supported by Penang State EXCO for Tourism and Creative Economy - PETACE)
core_facts.venue: Aspen Vision City, Batu Kawan (course over the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah Bridge, the Penang Second Bridge)

pros: The Second Bridge is closed to traffic for the race
A seven-hour marathon limit, with a medal and finisher tee for every finisher inside it
21 aid stations on the marathon, nearly all with water, 100 Plus and toilets
Prize money ten deep: 3:46:16 was tenth in the 2025 women's open marathon
Low entry fees: RM150 for the marathon at the 2025 general rate
cons: A 1.30am start in Batu Kawan means a late-night shuttle from George Town
Humid night air: 25°C with a 23°C dew point at the 2025 start, and little breeze
An out-and-back on one bridge, run mostly in the dark
Only two age groups, Open and Veteran
Getting into the start pens was confusing in 2025

faqs.question: When is the Penang Bridge International Marathon held?
faqs.answer: The race is on Sunday 13 December 2026, starting and finishing at Aspen Vision City in Batu Kawan on the Penang mainland. It is a night race: the organiser gives start times of 1.30am for the full marathon, 3am for the half marathon and 6.30am for the 10 km. The final race pack collection is at Aspen Vision City.

faqs.question: What distances can I run in this race?
faqs.answer: Runners choose from three distances: a 42.195 km full marathon, a 21.1 km half marathon or a 10 km run. All three go out and back over the Penang Second Bridge, not the first Penang Bridge; the full marathon reaches the island end near Bayan Lepas. Qualifying times are 7 hours, 3 hours 30 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes.

faqs.question: Who organises the Penang Bridge International Marathon?
faqs.answer: The event is organised by the Penang State Tourism Development office, with support from the Penang State EXCO for Tourism and Creative Economy (PETACE), and the course is certified by AIMS. The race moved to Batu Kawan and the Second Bridge in 2024 because of light rail construction on Penang island.
